Set Control Parameters for Simulation

Source: R/parameter_estimation.R
set_control_mcmc.Rd

The settings of the Langevin sampler that draws the latent effects of a binomial, Poisson or negative binomial model given the data, in glgpm() and predict().

Usage

set_control_mcmc(
  n_draws = 2000,
  burnin = 2000,
  thin = 10,
  h = NULL,
  c1_h = 1,
  c2_h = 0.6
)

Arguments

n_draws

Positive integer. The number of draws kept, after burn-in and thinning, on which fitted values and predictions are based. Default is 2,000. The chain runs burnin + n_draws * thin iterations.

burnin

Non-negative integer. The number of iterations discarded at the start of the chain, during which the step size is adapted. Default is 2,000.

thin

Positive integer. One iteration in thin is kept after burn-in. Default is 10.

h

Numeric. An optional positive step size for Langevin MCMC.

c1_h

Numeric. Positive scale for the burn-in Robbins-Monro step-size adaptation. Default is 1.

c2_h

Numeric. Exponent controlling the diminishing adaptation gain. Must be larger than 0.5 and no larger than 1. Default is 0.6.

Value

A list of class "RiskMap_control_mcmc" with n_draws, burnin, thin, h, c1_h and c2_h.

Details

During burn-in the step size of the Langevin chain is adapted towards an acceptance rate of 0.574, starting from h (by default \(1.65 / d^{1/6}\) for \(d\) latent effects). The step kept after burn-in is the geometric mean of the adapted step over the second half of burn-in.

The latent effects of a Gaussian model are drawn independently, so its predictions take n_draws draws without burn-in or thinning.

Seeds are not part of the control settings. Pass seed to glgpm(), predict.RiskMap(), assess_prediction() or assess_simulation().

See also

glgpm

Examples

# Default parameters (MCMC)
control_mcmc <- set_control_mcmc()

# Custom MCMC parameters: 600 draws from 3,000 + 600 * 20 iterations
control_mcmc <- set_control_mcmc(n_draws = 600, burnin = 3000, thin = 20)
